topic.title: Monte Carlo Planning and Search-Based Policy Improvement
topic.overview: Sampling-based planners evaluate possible futures without enumerating every action sequence. This topic includes Monte Carlo tree search, sequential Monte Carlo, Bayesian adaptation, and policy improvement through search. Recent work also studies branching over reasoning continuations, where the allocation of samples affects the accuracy of learning signals.
topic.whyItMatters: Search quality depends on where computation is spent, not only how many rollouts are generated. Parallel sampling and variance-aware allocation can make planning more scalable while preserving useful distinctions among candidate actions or thoughts.
topic.evolution: Earlier representatives combine heuristic search, game-tree evaluation, and temporal-difference learning. Later methods add Bayesian and maximum-entropy planning. The 2024–2026 evidence develops parallel particle-based policy optimization and analyzes why branching into multiple continuations can reduce an uncertainty floor that additional independent thoughts alone cannot remove.
openQuestions: How should a planner allocate samples between breadth and repeated evaluation of promising branches?
When do model errors invalidate apparent gains from deeper search?
